1:1.t: Before I take up Zephaniah, who is ninth in the order of the twelve prophets, it seems I must answer those who think I deserve to be laughed at because, passing over men, I write above all to you, O Paula and Eustochium. If they knew that Huldah prophesied while men were silent, and that Deborah, a judge and a prophetess alike, overcame the enemies of Israel while Barak was afraid; and that Judith and Esther, in a type of the Church, both slew the adversaries and delivered Israel, which was about to perish, from its peril; they would never crook their hand into a stork behind my back. I say nothing of Anna and Elizabeth and the other holy women, whose little fires, like those of the stars, the bright light of Mary hides. I will come to pagan women, so that they may see that even among the philosophers of the world it is the differences of minds, not of bodies, that are wont to be considered. Plato introduces Aspasia disputing; Sappho is written of together with Pindar and Alcaeus; […]

The word of the Lord which came to Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah. LXX likewise. The Hebrews hand down that whenever the father or grandfather of any prophet is set in the title, they too were prophets. Hence Amos also, one of the twelve prophets, who had said: I am not a prophet, nor the son of a prophet, but a herdsman of goats, plucking sycamore fruit, does not have his father's name in the title. If this is true, Zephaniah the prophet, whom we are now attempting to expound, was begotten by a prophetic custom, so to speak, and of a glorious stock of ancestors; for he had as father Cushi, as grandfather Gedaliah, as great-grandfather Amariah, as great-great-grandfather Hezekiah, and he himself, like the last charioteer, completed such a four-horse team. Some have translated the name of Zephaniah as 'watchtower', others as 'the secret of the Lord'. […]

1:2.t: But if we wish to understand something deeper as well — because of what is said by the Seventy: Let it fail with failing from the face of the earth —, and to take failing in a good sense, according to that saying: And failing, Abraham died in a good old age, an old man and full of days, and was gathered to his people; and from what Scripture relates of Isaac and Jacob, we shall see how they fail with failing from the face of the earth, and that they fulfil this precept: Who, having their conversation in heaven, and in the flesh not warring according to the flesh, because they know that those who live in the flesh cannot please God, do everything, as far as in them lies, that they may not be in the flesh but in the spirit; and withdrawing from the earth they say: He has raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ. […]

Gathering I will gather all things from the face of the earth, says the Lord, gathering man and beast, gathering the bird of the heaven and the fish of the sea; and there will be ruins of the ungodly, and I will destroy men from the face of the earth, says the Lord. LXX: Let it fail with failing from the face of the earth, says the Lord; let man fail and the cattle; let the birds of the heaven fail, and the fish of the sea; and the ungodly will be weakened, and I will remove the wicked from the face of the earth, says the Lord. What we have set down in the Seventy, And the ungodly will be weakened, was added from the translation of Theodotion; in its place Symmachus translated: And stumbling blocks with the ungodly, so that 'will be gathered' or 'will fail' is understood; and the Fifth Edition: And weakness with the ungodly will fail. We ought therefore, following our custom, first to weave the history, and afterwards to discuss the loftier things. […]

1:3.t: And what it had first said in general, Let it fail with failing from the face of the earth, divine Scripture afterwards divided into parts: let man fail, and the cattle, let the birds of the heaven fail, and the fish of the sea. There are four things which are commanded to fail: first man, the rational being, then three which are subject to man, the cattle, and the birds, and the fish, which I think are set down also in Psalm 8: Moreover also the beasts of the field, the birds of the heaven and the fish of the sea, which pass through the paths of the sea. But what it had first said: all sheep and oxen, it separated as the chief of the cattle, and did not wish to number them with the cattle that remained. So let man fail, let the cattle fail, let the birds of the heaven fail, let the fish fail; and it did not say: let the wild beasts fail, let the creeping things of the earth fail. For these ought not to fail but to perish; but let those things fail which can receive correction. […]

1:4.t: And I will stretch out my hand over Judah and over all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will destroy from this place the remnants of Baal, and the names of the temple-keepers with the priests, and those who worship the host of heaven upon the roofs, and worship and swear by the Lord, and swear by Milcom; and those who turn away from behind the Lord, and who have not sought the Lord nor searched for him. LXX: And I will stretch out my hand over Judah, and over all who dwell in Jerusalem; and I will remove from this place the names of Baalim, and the names of the priests with the priests, and those who worship the host of heaven upon the roofs, and those who swear by the Lord, and swear by their king, and those who turn aside from the Lord, and who do not seek the Lord, and who do not hold fast the Lord. […]

Both the temple-keepers, then, and those once priests of God, and those who on the housetops worshipped the host of heaven, the sun and the moon and the rest of the stars; and those who swore by the name of the Lord and by the name of the idol of the Ammonites, Milcom — which was turned by the LXX into 'king' —, the Lord will remove from the place of Jerusalem, or will destroy; for it is understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ (in common). And I will destroy from this place the remnants of Baal, and I will destroy the names of the temple-keepers with the priests, and I will destroy those who worship the host of heaven upon the roofs, and I will destroy those who worship and swear by the Lord, and swear by Milcom, and I will destroy those who turn away, or turn aside, from behind the Lord, and who do not seek him, or do not hold him fast. Now Israel turn away behind the Lord, who, abandoning his worship, swear by Milcom, and worship the host of heaven, and venerate Baal, the idol of the Sidonians. […]

1:7.t: Be silent before the face of the Lord God, for the day of the Lord is near, for the Lord has prepared a victim, he has sanctified his called ones. LXX: Fear before the face of the Lord God, for the day of the Lord is near, for the Lord has prepared his sacrifice, he has sanctified his called ones. Where the LXX translated fear, and we have set down be silent, in the Hebrew there is an interjection of one commanding silence, which the comic poets also often use; but silence is also enjoined absolutely on all, because the day of the Lord is to come. And by the day of the Lord let us understand the day of captivity and of vengeance on the sinful people, and the victim of the overthrow of Jerusalem, and the sanctification of those whom he has dedicated to slaughter, according to what is said in Jeremiah: Sanctify them for the day of their slaughter. And the sense is: The captivity foretold long ago is coming against the ungodly people; it is already near. For the prophecy is woven under King Josiah; […]

1:8.t: And it will be on the day of the Lord's victim, I will visit upon the princes, and upon the king's sons, and upon all who are clothed in foreign apparel. And I will visit everyone who arrogantly enters upon the threshold on that day, who fill the house of the Lord their God with iniquity and deceit. LXX: And it will be on the day of the Lord's victim, and I will take vengeance upon the princes, and upon the house of the king, and upon all who are clothed in alien garments; and I will take vengeance openly upon all who are in the porches on that day, who fill the house of the Lord their God with ungodliness and deceit. On the day of the Jewish captivity, when the whole people is to be sacrificed, the Lord will visit both upon the princes, who drank strong drink in the morning, and upon the king's sons, either all of the royal stock or certainly, properly, the sons of Josiah, whom we read were either killed or captured; […]

But since we have once begun to expound tropologically as well: The Lord will visit, at the coming and passion of the Savior, that is, on the day of the victim of his Son, upon the high priests and priests of the Jewish people and upon the royal house. For up to that time the kings of Judah from the stock of David continued, according to the prophecy of Jacob: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up, and he will be the expectation of the nations. For after the Lord's victim the kingdom was taken from the Jews. And upon all, he says, who are clothed in alien garments, who have withdrawn from the protection and clothing of God and are covered with their own error. And I will take vengeance openly upon all who are in the porches, that is, who have gone out from the temple of God; and though they ought to have been within, because of their sins they have gone outside and withdrawn from the Church of God, filling his temple with ungodliness and deceit. […]

1:9.t: And upon all who arrogantly enter upon the threshold on that day, that is, against the proud, who with a certain disdain and haughtiness of rank ascend the steps of the temple and the threshold of the sanctuary. Moreover, where we translated: Who arrogantly enter upon the threshold, it can be understood according to the Hebrew as 'who leap over the threshold'; and this is to be taken historically: I will avenge upon those who, according to the first book of Kingdoms (1 Samuel), do not tread on the threshold of the idols, serving superstitions, who have filled the house of the Lord their God not only with the worship of idols but with iniquity and crime and every lie, so that to the error of religion there might be joined also iniquity toward subjects and lying toward neighbours.

1:10.t: And it will be on that day, says the Lord, the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate, and wailing from the Second, and a great crushing from the hills. LXX: And it will be on that day, says the Lord, the sound of a cry from the gate of those who pierce, and wailing from the Second, and a great crushing from the hills. On the day of the Lord's victim, when he stretches out his hand over Judah and over all who dwell in Jerusalem, and a hostile army has besieged it, there will be the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate and wailing from the Second, and a great crushing from the hills. They called the Fish Gate the one which leads to Diospolis and Joppa, and of all the roads of Jerusalem it was the nearest to the sea; of it Ezra too relates: But the Fish Gate the sons of Hassenaah built; they covered it, and set up its doors and locks and bars. […]

1:11.t: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar; all the people of Canaan has fallen silent. LXX: Lament, you who inhabit the one cut to pieces, for all the people of Canaan has been made like. The Mortar, which in Hebrew is called machtes, and which was rendered by Aquila εὶς τὸν ὅλμον (into the mortar), must be read with its first syllable not short, lest we think it means σφαῖραν (a ball), but long, so that we may know it is said of the mortar in which grain is pounded, a hollow vessel, suited also to the use of physicians, in which, properly speaking, ptisans are usually crushed. Someone may say that he has understood what the Mortar means, but wishes to know why it has been taken up in the present place. Because there was once a description of the captured city, and it is said: A voice of crying from the Fish Gate, and wailing from the Second, and a great crushing from the hills; now the same order of description is kept, and the wailing is spoken of those who dwell in the valley of Siloam. […]

1:12.t: And it will be at that time, I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will visit upon the men settled on their lees, who say in their hearts: The Lord will not do good, and he will not do evil. LXX: And it will be on that day, I will search Jerusalem with a lamp, and I will take vengeance upon the men who despise their charges, and say in their hearts: The Lord will not do good, and he will not do evil. At the time and on the day of the captivity of Jerusalem, whether by the Babylonians or by the Romans — because she forsook the law of the Lord, and acted impiously against the Lord her Creator —, the Lord will search out with a lamp all the hidden places of Jerusalem, and will let no one escape unpunished. Let us read the histories of Josephus, and there we shall find it written that princes and kings and powerful men and priests, who had hidden themselves in them for fear of death, were dragged out of sewers too, and caves, and grottoes, and tombs. […]

1:13.t: The lust of possessions and money are not to be sought for. In Solomon, in Ecclesiastes: "He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver." Also in Proverbs: "He who holds back the corn is cursed among the people; but blessing is on the head of him that communicates it." Also in Isaiah: "Woe to them who join house to house, and lay field to field, that they may take away something from their neighbor. Will you dwell alone upon the earth?" Also, in Zephaniah: "They shall build houses, and shall not dwell in them; and they shall appoint vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them, because the Day of the Lord is near." Also in the Gospel according to Luke: "For what does it profit a man to make a gain of the whole world, but that he should lose himself?"
1:13.s: Treatise XII. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews, TESTIMONIES AGAINST THE JEWS 12:3.61

1:13.t: According to tropology, however, when the time of judgment comes, or of each one's death and departure from the world, then all their strength will be for plunder, so that what was strong for evil, and was lifted up against the Lord, may be made weak and broken and turned to something better. Just as, if someone plunders the strength of a robber and a pirate and a thief, and renders them weak, their weakness profits them; for with their limbs disabled, which they formerly did not use well, they will cease from evil work. As for what follows: And their house for a desert, there are many in the Church building Zion in blood and Jerusalem in iniquity, whom it profits that such houses be destroyed. Let us read Leviticus, where a leprous house is ordered to be destroyed. And because the leprosy is lasting and spreads, its stones and timbers and all its dust are ordered to be thrown outside the city into an unclean place. […]

And their strength will be for plunder, and their house for a desert. And they will build houses, and will not inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards, and will not drink their wine. Close is the great day of the Lord; it is close, and exceedingly swift. LXX: And their strength will be for pillage, and their houses will be scattered. And they will build houses, and will not dwell in them, and they will plant vineyards, and will not drink their wine, for close is the great day of the Lord; close and exceedingly swift. It is plain that in both captivities their whole army was cut down, and their houses torn down, and their fields and vineyards laid waste, and that the patience of God no longer put them off. But while they were saying to the prophets, this will be for a time, and for many days, the great day of the Lord came upon them, exceedingly swift.

1:14.t: Near is the great day of the Lord and exceedingly swift, which no one can withstand; and it is near either because of eternity, since nothing is long to it, or because of the greatness of the punishment, since to one who suffers it, the torment that is to be inflicted never seems far off. Or else it is near, as we said above, when we depart from the world, and each one's death has brought about the consummation of the world; and not only near, but also exceedingly swift, so that the swiftness of its coming may be shown in what is added, exceedingly.

But if, as above, we refer the day of the Lord to the consummation of the world, or to the end of each one's life, the interpretation will be plain: that the voice of the day of the Lord is bitter, and full of constraint and of wrath, and that the strong man is afflicted there, since even those who are holy are saved indeed, but yet so as through fire.

The voice of the day of the Lord is bitter; there the strong man will be afflicted.

That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of calamity and misery, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and whirlwind, a day of trumpet and clangor against the fortified cities and against the lofty corners. LXX: The voice of the day of the Lord is bitter and harsh; it has been set, strong. A day of wrath is that day, a day of tribulation and constraint, a day of misery and destruction, a day of darkness and whirlwind, a day of cloud and gloom, a day of trumpet and shouting against the fortified cities and against the lofty corners. In keeping with what precedes, take it either of the Babylonian captivity or of the last one, which they suffered at the hands of the Romans, over which the Lord also wept for Jerusalem, saying: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets, and stone those who are sent to you, and so on. […]

1:15.t: That day is a day of tribulation, and distress, and calamity, and misery, on which they will say: Woe to us, for we have become wretched. A day of darkness: For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, and it must be that darkness overtakes him who hates the light.

It will be a day of cloud and whirlwind; for the tempest of the Lord will come upon him, and the clangor of the trumpet which the Apostle signifies, saying: At the last trumpet. For it will be a day of trumpet and clangor against the fortified cities, which they had built for themselves with Cain in the multitude of their sins. And against the lofty corners: perverse works, turning aside from the right way of the Lord. Hence the Pharisees, ὑποκρίται (hypocrites), are also rebuked by the Savior, because they worship at the corners of the streets. For the way that is straight and tends toward paradise is narrow, and strait is the way which leads to life. But the way that is broken, having corners, and crooked, is broad and spacious, the way which leads to death. […]

But let them hear how the prophet Zephaniah holds out over them the power of divine rebuke, saying, Behold the day of the Lord cometh, great and horrible, the day of wrath, that day; a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of cloud and whirlwind, a day of trumpet and clangour, upon all fenced cities, and upon all lofty corners. For what is expressed by fenced cities but minds suspected, and surrounded ever with a fallacious defence; minds which, as often as their fault is attacked, suffer not the darts of truth to reach them? And what is signified by lofty corners (a wall being always double in corners) but insincere hearts; which, while they shun the simplicity of truth, are in a manner doubled back upon themselves in the crookedness of duplicity, and, what is worse, from their very fault of insincerity lift themselves in their thoughts with the pride of prudence? […]
1:15.s: The Book of Pastoral Rule, Part 3 (Admonition 12)

1:17.t: But at the consummation, whether of the world or of each one, all men will be afflicted who remained men and died as men. And they will walk like the blind, because they have lost the light of the virtues, and they will have no place for repentance; and they will suffer these things because they have sinned against the Lord. For if the Lord is justice, truth, holiness, and the other virtues, whoever has acted unjustly, and has lied, and has pursued harlots and vices, has sinned against the Lord. But what follows: And their blood will be poured out like soil, and their bodies like the dung of oxen, seems absurd, that we should say that in the resurrection of the dead, and at the consummation of the world and the judgment, blood is poured out and bodies lie like dung. Therefore what is said to Noah: And the blood of your souls I will require at the hand of all the beasts, and at the hand of man, and at the hand of his brother I will require the soul of man; […]

And I will afflict men, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord; and their blood will be poured out like soil, and their bodies like dung; but even their silver and gold will not be able to deliver them on the day of the wrath of the Lord; in the fire of his zeal the whole earth will be devoured, for he will make a consummation with haste for all who inhabit the earth. LXX: And I will afflict men, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord, and he will pour out their blood like dust, and their flesh like the dung of oxen, and their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them on the day of the wrath of the Lord; and in the fire of his zeal the whole earth will be consumed, for he will make a consummation and haste upon all who inhabit the earth. It is not difficult to say, according to the former sense, that Jerusalem suffered these things, which she endured because of the cross of the Lord; […]

On the day of consummation, therefore, whether general or particular, all the blood that has been poured out will cry to the Lord and will appear in the midst, and the works of blood and the earthly works will lie like dust and dung, and silver and gold will not be able to deliver the rich from the day of wrath, while he who dies hears: Fool, this night your soul will be taken from you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be? Not that we deny that gold and silver deliver the rich from death — For the ransom of a man's soul is his own riches —, but that they cannot deliver them at that time when they leave their riches behind of necessity. For the whole earth and all things that are earthly will be devoured by the zeal of the Lord. And when he says, by zeal, understand the Lord as still loving. For if he did not love the human soul, he would never be jealous over it, and, like a husband, take vengeance on the sin of his wife; for if he did not love her, he would not even be angry at her adultery. […]

1:18.t: I am weary and vexed at enumerating the multitude of ornaments, and I am compelled to wonder how those who bear such a burden are not worried to death. O foolish trouble! O silly craze for display! They squander meretriciously wealth on what is disgraceful and in their love for ostentation disfigure God's gifts, emulating the art of the evil one. The rich man hoarding up in his barns and saying to himself, "You have many goods laid up for many years; eat, drink be merry," the Lord in the Gospels plainly called "fool." "For this night they shall take your soul; whose then shall those things which you have prepared be?" Apelles, the painter, seeing one of his pupils painting a figure loaded with gold color to represent Helen, said to him, "Boy, being incapable of painting her beautiful, you have made her rich." Such Helens are the ladies of the present day, not truly beautiful but richly got up. […]

2:1.t: Come together, gather yourselves, unlovable nation, before the command brings forth the day like passing dust; before the wrath of the fury of the Lord comes upon you, before the wrath of the indignation of the Lord comes upon you. LXX: Be gathered and be collected together, untaught nation, before you are like a flower passing away in a day, before the wrath of the Lord comes upon you, before the day of the wrath of the fury of the Lord rushes upon you. After the description of the evils which are to come on the day of the Lord — according to the twofold explanation of the captivity which we gave above —, the people is called to repentance, and it is said to it: Come together, and gather yourselves, or, as is written in the LXX: Be collected together, that is, according to the Apostle, be bound to one another by the bond of charity, unlovable nation, you who are unworthy of the love of God, or untaught nation, of which it is said in Deuteronomy: A foolish people, and not wise, and in Jeremiah: In vain have I struck […]

2:3.t: Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth, who have wrought his judgment; seek the just one, seek the meek one, if somehow you may be hidden on the day of the fury of the Lord. For Gaza will be destroyed, and Ashkelon into a wilderness. Ashdod they will cast out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted. LXX: Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth; work judgment, and seek justice and answer them, that you may be protected on the day of the wrath of the Lord; for Gaza will be plundered, and Ashkelon into a wilderness; and Ashdod will be cast forth at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted. He is called humble of the earth who has been humbled not by humility, which signifies a virtue, but by sins, and cannot say with Christ: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart. For everyone who humbles himself will be exalted. And in another place the word is directed to the holy man: The greater you are, the more humble yourself, and before God you will find grace. […]

But according to the Seventy, the humble of the earth, of whom we spoke above, are commanded to work judgment and to seek justice, which I do not think is anything other than Christ. And because everyone who seeks will find, what they have found let them answer to others, that is, let them teach others: For wisdom hidden and a treasure that does not appear, what profit is there in both? And this, he says, I command you, that you may be protected on the day of the wrath of the Lord, either at the consummation of the world or at the departure of each one from this world.

2:4.t: But if he is in doubt about those who have done his judgments, saying: If somehow you may be hidden on the day of the fury of the Lord, what will become of sinners? For so great a devastation will come upon the land of Judea, and so lofty a conqueror, the Babylonian army, will come up hither, that the same captivity will seize even the most powerful cities of the Philistines, which always withstood you in equal combat. For Gaza will be destroyed, and Ashkelon will be reduced to desolation, and Ashdod they will drag into captivity not by stealth but by war, that is, in open daylight and by victory; and Ekron, which is interpreted uprooting, will undergo what its name signifies, that is, it will be uprooted. This is according to the letter and the Hebrew truth.

For Gaza and Ashkelon and Ashdod and Ekron will undergo different punishments. For Gaza is interpreted its strength. All, therefore, who applaud themselves in strength of body and worldly power, and say with the devil, By strength I will do it, will be plundered on the day of the wrath of the Lord and brought to nothing. Ashkelon also, which is called weighed, or murderous fire, when the day of the wrath of the Lord comes, will feel the measure of its crime and will be pressed down by the same weight with which it acted. And because it burned to shed blood, and caused many souls to stumble, and in it was fulfilled: The man of blood and deceit the Lord will abhor, it will not be plundered like Gaza, but, reduced to desolation, it will be burned to dust by the fires of Gehenna. Ashdod too, which in Hebrew is called esdod and in our language means fire of generation, will be laid waste in clear light; for it burned with lust and raged in the fire of generation. […]

2:5.t: But according to the spiritual sense and the translation of the LXX the understanding is difficult, especially since they also disagree in the interpretation. For where we translated nation of the lost, they said strangers of the Cretans; and where in Hebrew is written goi chorethim, for goi, that is, nation, they read car, that is, stranger; and chorethim, which means of the lost, they took for the name of the island of Crete. Indeed both Aquila and the Fifth Edition translated ἔθνος ὀλέθριον (a destructive nation); and Theodotion ἔθνος ὀλεθρίας (a nation of destruction); Symmachus too ἔθνος ὀλεθρευόμενον (a nation being destroyed), all of which agree with our translation.

Woe to you who inhabit the cord of the sea, nation of the lost; the word of the Lord is upon you, Canaan, land of the Philistines, and I will destroy you so that there is no inhabitant. And the cord of the sea will be a resting place of shepherds, and folds of flocks; and the cord will be his who has remained of the house of Judah; there they will feed, in the houses of Ashkelon they will rest at evening, for the Lord their God will visit them and will turn back their captivity. LXX: Woe to you who inhabit the cord of the sea, sojourners of the Cretans; the word of the Lord is upon you, Canaan, land of the foreigners, and I will destroy you from habitation. And Crete will be a pasture of shepherds, and a fold of flocks, and the cord of the sea will be for those who are left of the house of Judah; upon them they will feed in the houses of Ashkelon; after noon they will turn aside from the face of the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God will visit them and will turn back their captivity. […]

Again, where we said: And the cord of the sea will be a resting place of shepherds, and all the translators agreed with this translation, in the LXX is written: And Crete will be a pasture of the flock, and a fold of flocks. Therefore, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, and keeping to the path of the common edition that we once began, we ask whether we have read the name of Crete elsewhere in the holy Scriptures. And, unless I am mistaken, this is ready to hand: Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies. This testimony is true. Those who waver and are carried about by every wind of doctrine, in the deceit of men, in the craftiness of error, though they ought to have dwelt in the land of confession, that is, in the land of Judea, chose rather to be strangers of the Cretans, who are beaten this way and that by the various waves of the sea, and sound with Corybantian bronze, and are, according to the Apostle: Like a tinkling cymbal. […]

2:7.t: But what is read in the LXX, From the face of the sons of Judah, we have marked with an obelus, for it is neither in the Hebrew nor found in any of the translators, and it disturbs the context and the sense of the chapter; not that it would have been difficult to weave a meaning somehow even with this set down; but we have once for all resolved to follow the truth of the translation, and the judgment of the more learned reader rather than that of the crowd.

2:8.t: I have heard the reproach of Moab and the blasphemies of the sons of Ammon, with which they reproached my people, and they were magnified over their borders. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will be as Sodom, and the sons of Ammon as Gomorrah, a dryness of thorns and heaps of salt, and a wilderness for ever; the remnants of my people will plunder them; the residue of my nation will possess them. This will befall them for their pride, because they blasphemed and were magnified over the people of the Lord of hosts. Terrible is the Lord over them, and he will waste away all the gods of the earth, and men will worship him from their place, all the islands of the nations. LXX: I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the sons of Ammon, in which they reproached my people and were magnified over my borders. […]

But the man who is learned, and compares spiritual things with spiritual, and seeks not the things that are below but those that are above, and rises with Christ from the underworld, and, putting off the old man, is clothed with the new, will refer the reproaches of Moab and the blasphemies of the sons of Ammon to the masters of doctrines contrary to the Church, who themselves also seem to be of the stock of Abraham, and to have escaped the burning of Sodom and Gomorrah, and to dwell in little Zoar. But because their generation is in darkness, and they cannot look upon the light of truth — for they have turned aside from God the Father, which is interpreted from the names Lot and Moab —, and they have ceased to be sons of God, which is what my people means, and, conceived of incestuous unions in a dark cave, they came into being, therefore to this day, insulting the simplicity of the sons of Judah, they desire to magnify their own possession over its borders; […]

2:9.t: Therefore, because they have blasphemed me and reproached my people, I, the Lord of hosts, who am able to fulfil what I threaten, and the God of Israel, who myself suffer injury in my people, will make Moab to be as Sodom, and the sons of Ammon as Gomorrah. Let us read visions of this kind in Isaiah and Jeremiah, and we shall find the same things that we now read here. A dryness of thorns and heaps of salt, and a wilderness for ever: in its place the LXX, meaning I know not what, translated: Damascus torn up and left, deceived, unless I am mistaken, by the ambiguity of the word; for dryness, which in Hebrew is called mamasac, if its first letter mem is changed and daleth is taken, has the same remaining letters as Damascus too, and in place of the former word damasec can be read. But it is asked how these cities, that is, Moab and the sons of Ammon, have been reduced to Sodom and Gomorrah, and, like an aridity of thorns and heaps of salt, are not to be built up for ever? […]

Now what we said above, that Damascus is not found in the Hebrew, nor in any other translator, we shall prove also from the very order of Scripture. For to what he had said, I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the blasphemies of the sons of Ammon, he afterwards related: That Moab will be as Sodom, and the sons of Ammon as Gomorrah. As for what follows, then, And Damascus deserted, like a heap of the threshing floor, he ought also to have said something about Damascus beforehand, so that, just as he had said of the two nations, Moab will be as Sodom, and the sons of Ammon as Gomorrah, whose sins he had already stated before. So he would also have described either the reproaches or the blasphemies of Damascus, so that afterwards he might be seen to inflict punishment deservedly. But this very phrase too, Like a heap of the threshing floor, which in Greek is said ὡς θιμωνιὰ ἄλωνος, we think the LXX translated ἀλος, that is, of salt; […]

And so the Lord swore by himself, saying: As I live, says the Lord. And beautifully, to distinguish himself from the dead gods, who are called idols, the God of Israel, that is, of the people that sees God, says that he lives; whereas these blaspheming nations, that is, Moab and the sons of Ammon, of whom we said above: They will be as Sodom and Gomorrah, seem indeed to themselves, in that they are not Gentiles, to have come out of Sodom and Gomorrah; but because they blaspheme the people of God and act against Israel, they will be reckoned as Sodom and Gomorrah; and they will be blotted out as those were blotted out before, having in themselves no trace of greenness and life. Nor is it surprising if we understand this of heretics, that they are reckoned as Sodom and Gomorrah, since even to churchmen who have not observed the commandments of God and have gone out from his precepts it is said through Isaiah: Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom, and attend to the law of the Lord, people of Gomorrah. […]

And so Moab and Ammon and Damascus, which have prepared themselves against the knowledge of the Lord, and have blasphemed the people of God, and spoken very many insults against it, and wished to extend their borders in the land of the Church and to possess the people of God, will be deserted and destroyed; and the remnant of the people of God, that is, churchmen learned in the Lord's Scriptures, will plunder them, and the residue of the Lord's nation will possess them, and this will be to them for the insult with which they reproached and were magnified against the Lord Almighty. See the clemency, see the mercy of the Lord: he suffers insult, he is blasphemed, his borders are plundered, and what does he do? He sends to the remnant of his people, of whom we have spoken, that he may divide out for himself those who blaspheme him and lead them into his own possession. […]

Now let us return to the LXX translators, and let us compel the Jews, who follow only the history, to explain to us when Moab and the sons of Ammon became like Sodom and Gomorrah, and like heaps of salt, and deserted for ever; they must show the sulphurous rains, the vineyards, the land turned into ashes and embers, and that the sea which is now called Dead flooded over from what were once wells of salt, when the Jews plundered them, when the remaining Israelite peoples possessed them. Or what indignation of the Lord is it, for blasphemy and insults, to waste away and destroy them? Not Moab and Ammon, but the whole earth, so that they may worship him, each from his place, all the islands of the nations? This he will rather bestow on the blasphemers as a benefit, that they may return from error to salvation. But if they wish to say that after the return from Babylon these nations were subjected to the people of Israel, first we shall demand the authority of the Scriptures by which they may prove that this happened; […]

2:10.t: And this will befall them for their pride, because they blasphemed and were magnified against the people of the Lord of hosts; and this Lord of hosts will be terrible over them, and his terror will not kill the proud; he will not shed the blood of the blasphemers, but will destroy and waste away all their idols, so that those who before were held by error and did not perceive the benefits of the Lord, pressed by the necessity of evils, may know that idols profit nothing, and may worship him, each one from his place, all the islands of the nations. Thus far according to the Hebrew.

2:11.t:
And, therefore, our Lord and Saviour rightly says to those who suppose that God ought only to be worshipped in Jerusalem, or in certain mountains, or some definite places:

"1. The hour cometh and now is, when the true worshippers shall neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem worship the Father. For God is a Spirit, and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."

So He said, and presently, not long after, Jerusalem was besieged, the holy place and the altar by it and the worship conducted according to Moses' ordinances were destroyed, and the archetypal holiness of the pre-Mosaic men of God reappeared. And the blessing assured thereby to all nations came, to lead those who came to it from the first step and from the first elements of the Mosaic worship to a better and more perfect life. […]
2:11.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 1, Chapter 6

2:11.t: Suffice it to say now, that we must hold to the truth, that the prophecies have only been fulfilled after the coming of Jesus our Saviour. For it is through Him that in our day that old system of Abraham, the most ancient and venerable form of religion, is followed by the Egyptians, the Persians, the Syrians and the Armenians. The Barbarians from the end of the earth, those of them who were of old the most uncivilized and wild, yea, they that inhabit the isles, for prophecy thought well even to mention them, follow it as well. And who would not be struck by the extraordinary change—that men who for ages have paid divine honour to wood and stone and daemons, wild beasts that feed on human flesh, poisonous reptiles, animals of every kind, repulsive monsters, fire and earth, and the lifeless elements of the universe should after our Saviour's coming pray to the Most High God, Creator of Heaven and earth, the actual Lord of the prophets, and the God of Abraham and his forefathers? […]
2:11.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 1, Chapter 6

2:11.t: The Lord Almighty will therefore come and will be manifest over them, he whom they do not now know, of whom they are ignorant; and he will destroy all their doctrines, that is, their gods, and the idols of the various nations, so that, after the images which they had composed for themselves out of their own mind have been overthrown, the nations may turn to the Lord, and each one in his own place may worship him whom he did not know before.

Nor think that it was foretold that the nations should come unto some one place of God, in that it was said, "Unto Thee shall the nations come from the extremity of the earth." Understand, if you can, that unto the God of the Christians, Who is the Supreme and True God, the peoples of the nations come, not by walking but by believing. For the same thing was by another prophet thus foretold, "The Lord," saith he, "shall prevail against them, and shall utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth: and all the isles of the nations shall worship Him, each man from his place." Whereas the one says, "Unto Thee all nations shall come;" this the other says, "They shall worship Him, each man from his place." Therefore they shall come unto Him, not departing from their own place, because believing in Him they shall find Him in their hearts.

The Lord will come suddenly upon them, and will utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth, and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the nations! From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia shall they bring offering to me.

2:12.t: But if we note that in all the Scriptures those are called Ethiopians who are sunk deep in vices, according to what we read in Jeremiah: If the Ethiopian will change his skin, then, when the Ethiopians are converted to better things, there will be hope that no one who is willing to repent will be a stranger to salvation. Hence also the soul, at first polluted and stained with the filth of sins, says: I am black. And afterwards, at the end of the Song of Songs, it is written of that same soul, now cleansed and washed through repentance: Who is this who comes up made white; Moses too, that is, the spiritual law of the Lord, took to wife the Ethiopian woman from the nations. And Miriam, that is, the synagogue of the Jews, and Aaron, that is, the carnal priesthood, and not according to the order of Melchizedek, murmur against the law, but in vain. For at once the synagogue is drenched with leprosy, and, cast out of the camp, when the time is completed, at the prayer of Moses himself, she is brought back into the camp. […]

But you also, Ethiopians, will be slain by my sword; and he will stretch out his hand over the north and will destroy Asshur; and he will make the beautiful one a wilderness, and a pathless place, and as it were a desert. And flocks will lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations, and the pelican and the hedgehog will dwell on her thresholds; the voice of one singing in the window, the raven on the lintel, because I will wear away her strength. This is the glorious city, dwelling in confidence, which said in her heart: I am, and outside me there is no other any more; how has she been made a desert, a lair of beasts? Everyone who passes through her will hiss and will move his hand. LXX: And you, Ethiopians, will be wounded by my sword; and I will stretch out my hand over the north and I will destroy the Assyrian; and I will make Nineveh a wilderness, and waterless as a desert. And flocks will feed in the midst of her, and all the beasts of the earth; […]

2:13.t: After this it is not the Lord who speaks, as above, but the prophetic spirit speaks about him: And he will stretch out his hand over the north, and will destroy Asshur. The north, of which Jeremiah wrote: From the north evils will blaze up upon all the inhabitants of the earth. And of which Solomon makes mention: The north wind is a harsh wind, but by name it is called the right. And God stretches out his hand, the hand that inflicts punishments, for this reason: that both the north may feel the penalties, and those who are in its land, to which, according to Zechariah, the black horses go, of which it is said: There were black horses, they were going into the land of the north. And fittingly, whoever has moved his feet and withdrawn from the East, of which the same prophet says: Behold a man, the East is his name, and has looked toward the west, goes at once toward the north, which is not the right, but by name is called the right. […]

Moreover, what follows about Nineveh laid waste: And flocks will feed in her, and all the beasts of the earth, chameleons, and hedgehogs will lie down in her stalls, and beasts will rest in her hinges, and ravens in her windows, and so on, seems to me to have to be understood in accordance with what is written either in Jonah or in the prophet Nahum. And in Jonah indeed we interpreted Nineveh, that is, the beautiful one, which repented at the preaching of Jonah, that is, of the dove, as the Church gathered from the nations. In Nahum, however, we tempered the interpretation toward the world; and concerning the world, indeed, it is not difficult to interpret and to say that, when the Ethiopians have been wounded by the sword of the Lord, and he has stretched out his hand over the north, and has destroyed the Assyrian, the prince of the world, the world itself too perishes with its prince, and is reduced to the utmost desolation, and is pitiable to no one, but all hiss at its ruin and move their hands. […]

2:15.t: Everyone who passes through her will hiss and will move his hands. But if we understand this of the angels, we will interpret it thus: when the angels pass through her, and do not remain in her, as they had been accustomed to do before, they will be stunned and will marvel, and will not prop her up nor hold her up with their hand as she falls, but will lift up their hands and pass on through. Or else with a hiss they will raise their hands, and, as though lamenting in the manner of mourners, they will clap them together. If, however, we wish to take this of the devil and his angels, who also laid waste the vine that had been transplanted out of Egypt, we will say that through the soul from which Christ has withdrawn, and which before had been the temple of God and has ceased to be so, the serpent passes, and hisses in it, and vomits out the venoms of his malice, and not only does this, but also moves his works, which τροπικῶς (figuratively) are called hands. […]

3:1.t: Woe, provoking and redeemed city, the dove. She did not hear the voice, and did not accept discipline; she did not trust in the Lord, she did not draw near to her Lord. Her princes in the midst of her, like roaring lions; her judges, wolves of the evening, they left nothing for the morning. Her prophets mad, faithless men. Her priests have polluted the holy, they have acted unjustly against the law. The just Lord in the midst of her will not do iniquity. In the morning, in the morning he will give his judgment in the light, and it will not be hidden; but the unjust one knew no confusion. I have destroyed the nations, and their corners have been scattered; I have made their ways deserted, because there is no one who passes; their cities have been made desolate, with no man remaining, nor any inhabitant. I said: Yet you will fear me, you will accept discipline, and her dwelling will not perish because of all the things in which I visited her. Nevertheless, rising at dawn, they corrupted all their thoughts. […]

But the illustrious city, redeemed by the blood of Christ, is clearly understood, in keeping with what was said above, as the Church, which is also called a dove because of the simplicity of the multitude of believers within her.

Nor let it disturb anyone, as I have often said already, that I interpret these things as spoken against the Church, since he knows that in the holy Scriptures Jerusalem always bears the type of the Church; whoever sins away from her is either led off into Babylon, or, if he chooses of his own accord to go down to Jericho, is wounded by robbers. For what is so illustrious as the Church, which has been founded in the whole world, so redeemed by the blood of Christ, and a dove because of the grace of the Holy Spirit, as the Church gathered from the nations? In her very many who say that they believe in Christ have neither heard his voice, nor received discipline, nor wished to be near him.

3:2.t: She did not hear the commandment of the Lord, and when rebuked she would not accept discipline; nor, when evils pressed upon her, did she ever trust in the Lord her God; nor did she walk behind him; nor, when he said: I am the Lord who draws near, and not from afar, was she herself willing to draw near to him.

She did not hear the voice of the Lord, nor was she willing to accept discipline, nor did she trust in the Lord, because she would not draw near to the Lord her God so as to merit pardon of sins. For in vain does anyone say that he hears the voice of the Lord his God and trusts in the Lord, when he destroys faith by his works, and is joined to mammon more than to the Lord his God, and approaches him with a double heart, and believes that he can serve as a soldier under two masters, the world and God.

3:3.t: Her princes are like roaring lions. We have no doubt about the roaring and the ranging of lions when we see her princes thunder so against the peoples subject to them, and crush the common people with a tyrant's voice and rabid abuse, that you would think it not a shepherd among his flock, but a lion gnashing its teeth among the little sheep. Her judges too are like wolves of Arabia, killing in the evening and leaving nothing for the morning; not looking toward the rising of the sun, but lingering always in darkness, and turning the small possessions of the Church, and the things brought as offerings to God, to their own gain, so that the poor have nothing to eat in the morning; they lay everything waste as if in the night, with no one seeing; and when, after the manner of wolves, they plunder everything, they do not leave even small portions of food to the needy.

As for the saying: Her princes in her like roaring lions, I know that I will offend very many, because I interpret these things of bishops and elders, though the wicked elders who desired to violate Susanna do not condemn the other elders who have lived well. And the wicked princes whom the prophetic word describes are no reproach to good princes: For when a fool is scourged, the senseless man will be wiser; but if the senseless man becomes wiser, how much more he who is wise? But her judges and princes, taking gifts and selling justice, are they not rightly called wolves of Arabia, or evening wolves, as Symmachus translated? For they do not deserve to be called wolves of Benjamin, which seize prey in the morning and at evening give food, but evening wolves, which eat by night and leave nothing for the morning.

Her princes and judges and prophets and priests are also described, so that in the city we may understand the people, and in these titles of rank that I have mentioned, the leading men. Her princes, therefore, like lions, were always busy with plunder and with shedding the blood of their subjects; her judges were rapacious, leaving to others nothing they could seize. Her prophets, raving or astounded, which in Hebrew is said phoezim, and Aquila translated θαμβευταὶ (the astonished), spoke as if from the mouth of the Lord, and proclaimed everything against the Lord; the priests committed sacrilege in the place of the sanctuary, and while they acted against the law, they offered sacrifices according to the law.

3:4.t: Her prophets also, that is, the teachers who think that they teach the peoples and discourse on the Scriptures, πνευματοφόροι, that is, bearing the spirit, or spiritual — and this is to be read εἰρονικῶς (ironically) —, are men who are despisers; for what befits the Church is not to teach but to do, not to destroy words by deeds. But you, when you teach another and do not do it yourself, are to be called not so much a teacher as a despiser, of whom it is also written in Habakkuk: Look, you despisers, and behold, and wonder at the wonders, and perish. The priests too, who serve the Eucharist and distribute the blood of the Lord to his peoples, act impiously against the law of Christ, thinking that it is the words of the one who prays that make the εὐχαριστίαν (the Eucharist), not his life, and that only the solemn prayer is necessary, and not the merits of the priests, of whom it is said: And a priest in whom there is any blemish shall not approach to offer offerings to the Lord.

As for what follows: Her prophets πνευματοφόροι, that is, bearing the spirit, men who are despisers, let it disturb no one that, interpreting this of teachers, we call the same men both prophets and despisers, since the Apostle too commands: Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed in the day of redemption. And David says in Psalm 50 (51): Do not take your Holy Spirit from me. For unless the Holy Spirit, when grieved, were accustomed to flee his former lodging and to abandon his dwelling, Paul would never have commanded what I said above, nor would David after his adultery have dreaded lest he lose what he had received; of which it is also written to the Hebrews: How much worse punishments do you think he deserves who has trampled on the Son of God, and has held unclean the blood of the covenant, in which he was sanctified, and has done insult to the spirit of grace? […]

3:5.t: Therefore, because they acted unjustly, the just Lord will not do iniquity, but will render to the most wicked city what it deserves. In the morning, in the morning, that is, openly and without any ambiguity, he will pass judgment on her, and there will be nothing that can be hidden from him. And the Lord will do this so that the city, rebuked, may be converted to the better. But unjust Israel did not recognize its confusion, nor did it understand that the blows were inflicted on it for this purpose, that it might repent.

Though the princes, judges, prophets, priests of Jerusalem do these things, the Lord is nonetheless merciful and just. Merciful, in that he does not withdraw from his Church; just, in that he renders to each one what he deserves. For after the morning has come, and the night of this age has passed, he will give his judgment in the light, and neither he himself nor his judgment will be hidden.

And when he begins to demand from each one the money he had entrusted to them, he will not be unjust, nor will he make injustice prevail for ever, but he will pull down the proud princes, whom God resists, from their seats and from the height they held, and their corners will be scattered, that is, their perverse wills, turning aside from the straight road, corners in which the Pharisees too were always accustomed to pray, having despised the corner stone. But I think that it benefits the proud too to be pulled down from their arrogance, and to have their alleys and corners scattered, so that afterwards they may walk on the straight road. Then follows: And I will make their ways deserted, because there is no one who passes through, according to what is written in Psalm 1: And the way of the impious will perish. […]

3:6.t: I have avenged you, he says afterwards, on the nations, and I have destroyed their empires, so that you who had not perceived me through blows might at least know me through benefits. Or else it is to be understood thus: I have destroyed all your cities, O Judah, and all the villages and tribes subject to you, and the various borderlands, and so great was the desolation of men that there was no one to dwell in your cities; and after I did this, I sent my prophets, rising at dawn and calling to repentance, and I said: I have indeed done these things to you, O Jerusalem, but I did them that you might fear me, and accept discipline, and that your dwelling, that is, the temple, might not perish because of all the crimes you had committed. […]

3:7.t: And lest anyone think that we do violence to Scripture, let him learn from what follows. But I did these things, he says, that I might say to them: Behold, the paths of malice have been destroyed; from now on fear me, and learn discipline, lest my discipline also perish, finding in you no fruit of conversion, and all the things by which I wished to correct you be in vain, and that word which is written in Jeremiah may be applied to you: In vain have I struck your sons; you have not accepted discipline. Or else: Fear me, and receive discipline, so that all things may not perish from the sight of Jerusalem, nor she be brought utterly to desolation over these evils with which I threatened her.

Moreover, what we have expounded according to the Hebrew, Nevertheless, rising at dawn, they corrupted all their thoughts, in place of which it is written in the Seventy: Prepare yourself, rise up at dawn, all their foliage has been scattered, since it differs much from the Hebrew, and according to the LXX seems rather to agree with what follows, we will expound in what follows.

But we, who follow not the letter that kills but the spirit that gives life, nor Jewish fables, hear from the Lord: Prepare yourself, rise at dawn: all their clusters have been scattered, and, prepared, we say: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. And we hear the command in Proverbs: Prepare your works for your going out. And that which is said in a sacred manner in Leviticus, where in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, Aaron offers for the people the scapegoat, and that a living one, and, laying his hands upon its head, calls down upon it all the sins of the people of Israel, and hands it over into the hands of a prepared man, and sends it into the desert, this we understand of ourselves, and, preparing ourselves at the command of the true priest, we remove evil from the midst of the Church. And when we have done these things, the night passes, the day draws near, and, walking honestly as in the day, we say: O God, my God, to you I keep watch from the dawn. […]

3:8.t: And, promising us a reward for all these things, God says: Wait for me on the day of my resurrection for a testimony; for after vices and sins God will rise again in us. And according to what he commands in another place: Be my witnesses, and I am a witness, says the Lord God, and the servant whom I have chosen, the Father with the Son and the Holy Spirit is a witness for us, so that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand. And it seems to me that the sentence stands rather in this way, and that the truth is confirmed under these three witnesses, rather than through the letter. For there were two witnesses against Susanna, and against the Lord Savior himself, and yet the word did not stand in their mouth. Against Naboth, too, almost the whole city bore witness, and the agreement of most wicked witnesses had not the firmness of truth but the conspiracy of a crime. […]

Therefore wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my resurrection in the future; for my judgment is to gather the nations and to collect the kingdoms, to pour out upon them my indignation, all the wrath of my fury; for in the fire of my zeal all the earth will be devoured, because then I will restore to the peoples a chosen lip, that all may call upon the name of the Lord and serve him with one shoulder. LXX: Therefore wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my resurrection for a testimony, for my judgment is upon the gatherings of the nations, that I may receive kings, that I may pour out upon them all my wrath, the wrath of my fury; for in the fire of my zeal all the earth will be consumed, for then I will turn among the peoples a tongue into its generations, that all may call upon the name of the Lord, that they may serve him under one yoke. […]

It should be noted, however, that in the place where we translated: I will restore to the peoples a chosen lip, instead of chosen the Seventy said: into its generation, so that of the earth is to be understood. And the error arose from this, that the Hebrew word barura, which Aquila and Theodotion translated as chosen and Symmachus as pure, the Seventy read as badura, thinking the letter res (resh) to be daleth, because of the excessive similarity of the character, which is distinguished by a small stroke. And likewise, where we translated: On the day of my resurrection in the future, all the others too translated: for a testimony. The Hebrew who instructed me in the Scriptures maintained that laed in the present passage ought to be understood rather as εἰς ἔτι, that is, for the future, than as for a testimony. For Ed, which is written with the letters ain and daleth, is understood as ἔτι and μαρτύριον, that is, both the future and a testimony. […]

For that they were to be caught in Christ's net, He teacheth thee where He saith by one of the holy prophets, "For this wait for Me, saith the Lord, until the day of My rising up to bear witness, because My judgment is for the congregations of the heathen." For when Christ rose from the dead, He bestowed on those that were in error that judgment which is for their happiness and salvation. For He even commanded the holy disciples, "Go make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: and teaching them to observe all those things that I have commanded you."
3:8.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

3:9.t: And if it was true long ago: "Jacob is become the portion of the Lord, and Israel the rope of his inheritance." Yet afterwards it was also said that all the nations would be given to the Lord for His inheritance, the Father saying to him : " Desire of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance." And it is also prophesied that He shall rule from sea to sea and to the ends of the world : "All the Gentiles shall serve him, and in him shall the tribes of the earth be blessed." And the reason of this was that the Supreme God should make known His salvation before all nations. And I have already noted before that the name of Jesus translated from Hebrew into Greek would give "salvation," so that "the salvation of God" is simply the appellation of our Saviour Jesus Christ. […]
3:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

3:9.t:
[Passage quoted, Zeph. iii. 9.]

And in this passage the Lord promised that there will be left for Him a people meek and lowly, meaning none others but they of the Circumcision who believed in His Christ. And He again proclaimed that only the remnant of Israel should be saved, with those called from the other nations, as He shewed in the beginning of the prophecy.
3:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

3:9.t: And then I will turn upon the peoples a tongue into its generation, so that each one, having laid aside error, may return to the ancient speech of confessing the Lord, and at the name of Jesus every knee shall bend, of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth, and every tongue confess the Lord Jesus in the glory of God the Father. And casting away the bricks and the bitumen which we had in place of stones and clay, with which we were building up the pride of our error against the Lord, let us recover the tongue which we lost before, and let us be under the yoke of Christ, who says: My yoke is sweet, and my burden is light.

Because bodily action is carried on by the shoulder and the arm, if the good things which he put forth with the lips he did not fulfil in deed, he wishes to himself 'the shoulder to fall,' and 'the arm to be broken in pieces.' As though he said in plain words, 'If the things that I said I refused to do, this very member of my body, which was given to me for working withal, may I lose, that surely that may fall from the body which I would not exercise to advantage.' But if this sentence of a curse is to be referred to a spiritual meaning, it is doubtless plain that the arm is joined to the body by the shoulders, and as by the arm good practice, so by the shoulder the knitting together of social life, is denoted. Whence too the Prophet, regarding the holy peoples of the Church universal, that should serve God in concord, says, And they shall serve Him with one shoulder.
3:9.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 21.33

3:10.t: Beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, from there my suppliants, the sons of my dispersed ones, will bring a gift to me. On that day you will not be confounded over all your devices by which you have transgressed against me; for then I will take away from your midst the boastful ones of your pride, and you will no more be exalted on my holy mountain. And I will leave in your midst a poor and needy people, and they will hope in the name of the Lord. The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity, nor speak a lie; and a deceitful tongue will not be found in their mouth, for they will feed and lie down, and there will be none to terrify. LXX: From the ends of the rivers of Ethiopia I will receive my dispersed ones; they will bring sacrifices to me. On that day you will not be confounded by all your devices by which you have acted impiously against me, for then I will take away from you the disparagement of your insolence, and you will no more be magnified upon my holy mountain; […]

But we, taking from this fable the occasion of a true history, will say that, once a chosen lip, or a pure and white one, as Symmachus translated, has been restored to us, we leave behind in the rivers of Ethiopia all the blackness of the soul, and the foul colour, and the venom of the dragon, with which we had been dyed by vices and sins, and the masters of perverse doctrines by whom we were formerly watered, and that we, with the once-dispersed Israel, will bring gifts to Christ.

3:11.t: On that day, that is, when the multitude of the nations has believed, you too will not be utterly confounded over all your errors by which you transgressed against me, by choosing Barabbas and crucifying the Son of God. Then I will take away from your midst the scribes and priests and Pharisees, the boastful ones of your pride, and you will by no means boast any longer on my holy mountain, but you will have a poor people, unlettered men and fishermen, who will hope in the name of the Lord.

On that day, on which the light of Christ has risen for us, it will be said to each one of us: You will not be confounded by all your devices, namely the most wicked thoughts by which we acted impiously against the Lord; and all the pride and insolence will be taken away through which we were raised up against the Lord and against the mountain, his holy one, our Lord and Savior; and in place of proud and vain names a meek and humble people will be left in us, so that we may think nothing arrogant, nothing swollen, nothing that displeases God. And at the same time consider that on the day of judgment and in the consummation of the world all the names of dignities will be taken away, and one people will remain, and a flock under the good shepherd, which is meek and humble.

3:13.t: The remnant of Israel, not the multitude that cried out: Crucify, crucify him, not the high priests and the nobles, but the remnant, will by no means do iniquity, nor speak a lie in Christ, since they believe the truth; nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth, since they know that every lie is from the devil; for they will feed and will say: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing; in a place of pasture, there he has set me. Beside the water of refreshment he has brought me up; he has turned my soul; and there will be none to terrify, as the faith of believers overcomes the pride of persecutors. Let this be understood of the first coming of Christ, which the Jews promise themselves at the end; and they hope that they will dwell in Jerusalem, and, after the manner of cattle, will be filled with the bodily gifts and riches of Judah and fed on green grass, and that, when all the nations have been destroyed and made subject to them, no one can remain who might terrify them.

Then also the people of Israel, when the fullness of the nations has come in, for God has shut up all under sin, that he may have mercy on all, will fear the name of the Lord. And the remnant of Israel will no longer do the iniquity through which they denied the Lord, nor speak vain things, promising themselves foolish fables; nor will a tongue of lying be found in their mouth, since Christ, who is the truth, speaks through them. For then they too will feed in one flock, and will lie down in the Church, and will not fear the onslaughts of the true Nebuchadnezzar. Seeing and reading these things, such great mysteries, let us cry out with the Apostle and say: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God, how inscrutable are your judgments, and your ways unsearchable. […]

3:14.t: Take heart, O Jerusalem, the Lord will take away your iniquities. The Lord will wash away the filth of his sons and daughters by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning. He will pour upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your sins. Choiring angels shall encircle you, chanting, "Who is it that comes up all white and leaning upon her beloved?" For the soul that was formerly a slave has now accounted its Lord as its kinsman, and he, acknowledging its sincere purpose, will answer, "Ah, you are beautiful, my beloved, ah, you are beautiful … your teeth are like a flock of ewes to be shorn"—a sincere confession is a spiritual shearing. And further: "all of them big with twins," signifying the twofold grace, either that perfected by water and the Spirit or that announced in the Old and in the New Testament. […]

But according to the Hebrew, the Church is commanded to praise, and Israel, seeing God with the mind, to shout for joy, and the place of peace to exult and be glad with all its heart, to which it was said: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you.

Finally, let us consider the order of the reading, and we shall see that what is said pertains not to the Jews but to the Church of Christ. For after what had gone before: My judgment is upon the gatherings of the nations, that I may receive kings, up to the place where he says: That all may call upon the name of the Lord, and serve him under one yoke, and: Beyond the rivers of Ethiopia I will receive among my dispersed ones those who will bring me sacrifices; and after the remnant of the people of Israel, believing in Christ and saved, of whom it is said: And those who are left of Israel will fear the name of the Lord, and there will be none to terrify them. The Holy Spirit, preaching of the general consummation of the world, speaks: Rejoice, daughter of Zion, proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem, rejoice and delight with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. […]

Praise, daughter of Zion, shout for joy, Israel; be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord has taken away your judgment, he has turned away your enemies; the King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you will not fear evil any more. On that day it will be said: Jerusalem, do not fear, Zion; let your hands not be weakened. The Lord your God in your midst, the mighty one, he will save; he will rejoice over you with gladness, he will be silent in his love for you; he will exult over you with praise. Triflers (nugas) who withdrew from the law I will gather, because they were of you, so that you may no longer have reproach over them. LXX: Rejoice, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem; exult and delight with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord has taken away your iniquities, he has redeemed you from the hands of your enemies; the King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you will not see evils any more. […]

These things, meanwhile, if we wish to take them of the second coming of the Savior. Moreover, since the prophet Zechariah exhorts Zion and Jerusalem to a similar gladness, and Matthew says that this very prophecy was fulfilled in the first coming of Christ, we are compelled by necessity, or rather led by the very order of truth, to hope for what is said in Zephaniah not as future but as done. For it is written in Zechariah: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, just and a savior, himself humble and mounted upon a beast of burden and a new colt. Let these things have been said according to the Seventy.

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem; the Lord hath taken away thine iniquities. The King of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee; thou shalt not see evil any more. All things are more especially applicable to the Lord Christ.

3:15.t: For at the end and in the consummation of the world he has taken away her judgment, by no means judging and rebuking her, but saving her, and he has turned away her enemies, the hosts of demons. The King of Israel, the Lord, will be in her midst; she will not fear evil any more.

3:16.t: On that day, says the Lord, as we see peace and are set on high, let your hands not be weakened, he who also said through Isaiah: Be strengthened, weakened hands, and let your works be strong.

On that day it will be said to Jerusalem the free, who is not in slavery with her children, but who is the mother of the saints: Do not fear, Zion, for she herself is also Jerusalem; your works will by no means be weakened, nor will you do things which you will mourn having done.

3:17.t: The Lord your God, who will save you, mighty and powerful, will himself dwell in your midst; he will rejoice over you with exultation and gladness, and will keep silent about your sins in the love with which he loved you; and he will exult over you with praise, either because you are praiseworthy or because you sing with your praises.

For the mighty Lord, whom no one can resist, your savior, will himself restore to you the gladness which you lost, and, the old man cast away, will make you walk in the new, and he will do these things in his love, not by your merit but by his mercy. And he will rejoice in you and delight, receiving your salvation as the richest victim of your solemnity; and he himself will say to you: I will gather your crushed ones. A heart, indeed, crushed and humbled God will not despise, and: A crushed reed he will not break.

3:18.t: Triflers (nugas), or, as Aquila translated, those carried away, who withdrew from you, I will gather, because they were of you; that is: Those who through vices and sins had fled from your bosom and had come under the power of demons will come to you when the state of all things has been restored, and you will by no means suffer reproaches any longer over your lost sons. What we have rendered nugas, let us know that in the Hebrew it is the Latin word itself, and for that reason it was set down by us just as it stood in the Hebrew, so that we may know that the Hebrew tongue is the mother of all tongues, a matter which it is not the time to discuss now. But I wonder that Aquila and the Seventy, where we translated they were, namely in the place where we said: I will gather, because they were of you: instead of they were chose to translate woe, or ὄι, which Aquila always uses not for lamenting but for calling and crying out. […]

But since our hope is certain and the vows of the Jews are empty, let us now weave the present and last chapter according to the former understanding, and bring forward a testimony from Jesus son of Sirach: He who throws a stone on high throws it upon his own head. For since Zion and Jerusalem are set on high, whoever disparages Zion and Jerusalem and throws at her the stones of insults hurls them upon his own head, and his reproach will return upon his own head: And his pain and his iniquity will come down upon his crown. How many today reproach the soul that pursues the mysteries of God and wishes to see his peace, and say: He is mad, and drunk, and full of new wine; he flees the gatherings of men; he spurns delights, counts gold as mud, loves poverty alone. But those who are unbelievers reproach him even with the cross of Christ, and if ever they see him in distress and in temptation, they say: Where are your mercies, and the works of justice which you have performed? […]

3:19.t: Woe therefore to him who has taken up and undertaken reproach, and has bound himself over to such a task as to disparage Zion and the city of God, for the Lord is the avenger of this injury to his city, and he will say to Zion: Behold, I will act in you for your sake, that is, I will carry out your vengeance, and I will save the afflicted one, or, as it is said in the Greek, the pressed one, so that the sense is: I will save her who at present, like the grape and the olive, has been so pressed and afflicted by temptations and pressures, as by the winepress and the beam, that she might make wine and oil, and that Jesus might drink of the wine in the kingdom of his Father, and be anointed with the oil above his fellows. I think that it was for the pressing out of such wine and oil that Job suffered many things, and that, after he had made the wine and the oil, he heard from the Lord: Do you think that I answered you otherwise than that you might appear just? […]

Behold, I will kill all who have afflicted you at that time, and I will save the lame one, and her who had been cast out I will gather; and I will set them for praise and for a name in all the land of their confusion. At that time when I will bring you in, and at the time when I will gather you; for I will give you for a name and for praise to all the peoples of the earth, when I have turned back your captivity before your eyes, says the Lord. LXX: Behold, I will act in you, for your sake, at that time, and I will save the pressed one, and the rejected one I will receive, and I will set them in glory; and named in all the earth. And they will be confounded at that time when I have done well to you; and at the time when I have received you, for I will give you named and in glory among all the peoples of the earth, when I have turned back your captivity before you, says the Lord. […]

3:20.t: At that time, he says, when the pressed and rejected one has been received, and her sons set in glory — for the Lord glories in his athletes when he sees them crowned, as he gloried over Job against the devil; hence the Apostle too, exulting in the progress of his disciples, says: Yes, by your glory — those who had been your adversaries and had brought reproach against you will be confounded; and then they will see that those whom they had thought wretched are happy, and that those whom they reckoned poor and cast down have become powerful and glorious; then they will see their captivity, through which in this age they had been subjugated under a harsh rule, brought back into the heavenly Jerusalem, and themselves rising again to reproach and to everlasting confusion. Grant to us, Jesus Christ, who are pressed and afflicted and rejected in this age, that you may receive us and set us in glory; […]
